questions.q: Which of the following processes describes the postmortem cooling of the body to the ambient temperature?
questions.explain: Algor mortis is defined as the cooling of the body postmortem until it matches the environmental (ambient) temperature.
questions.exam: HOSA Forensic Science: Crime Scene & Death Investigation
questions.subject: Forensic Science

questions.q: A medical examiner notes a purplish discoloration on the victim's back where blood has pooled due to gravity. This physical condition is known as:
questions.explain: Livor mortis, or lividity, is the pooling of blood in the lowest parts of the body caused by gravity after the heart stops pumping.
questions.exam: HOSA Forensic Science: Crime Scene & Death Investigation
questions.subject: Forensic Science

questions.q: In a temperate climate, approximately how long after death does livor mortis typically become permanently fixed?
questions.explain: Lividity generally begins to show 2 hours after death and typically becomes fixed (permanent even when the skin is pressed) after about 8 hours.
questions.exam: HOSA Forensic Science: Crime Scene & Death Investigation
questions.subject: Forensic Science

questions.q: A body is discovered lying flat on its back, but lividity is present strictly on the victim's chest and stomach. What does this forensic evidence indicate?
options: The victim had internal bleeding in the chest cavity.
The victim died of a sudden heart attack.
The victim's body was moved from a face-down position to a face-up position after lividity became fixed.
The body is less than 2 hours dead.
questions.explain: If lividity does not match the body's resting position, it indicates the body was kept in a different position long enough for livor mortis to fix (typically 8+ hours) before being moved to its discovered position.
questions.exam: HOSA Forensic Science: Crime Scene & Death Investigation
questions.subject: Forensic Science

questions.q: What causes the physiological phenomenon known as rigor mortis?
options: The depletion of ATP (adenosine triphosphate) in muscle fibers, preventing muscle relaxation.
The rapid coagulation of blood in the veins.
Bacterial decomposition in the intestinal tract.
A sharp decrease in core body temperature freezing the tissues.
questions.explain: Rigor mortis (stiffening of muscles) occurs because cellular respiration ceases. Calcium builds up in muscle fibers, and without the continued production of ATP to release the myosin from actin filaments, the muscles become permanently contracted until the tissue begins to decay.
questions.exam: HOSA Forensic Science: Crime Scene & Death Investigation
questions.subject: Forensic Science

questions.q: At approximately what time after death does rigor mortis generally reach its peak (maximum stiffness) across the entire body?
questions.explain: Under normal conditions, rigor mortis begins within 2 hours, reaches its peak or maximum stiffness at approximately 12 hours, and then gradually dissipates.
questions.exam: HOSA Forensic Science: Crime Scene & Death Investigation
questions.subject: Forensic Science

questions.q: Investigators locate a body that exhibits no rigor mortis anywhere. Based ONLY on the timeline of rigor mortis, what is the most scientifically sound conclusion?
options: The victim has been dead exactly 12 hours.
The victim has either been dead for less than 2 hours or more than 36 to 48 hours.
The victim died due to poisoning, which prevents rigor mortis entirely.
The ambient temperature is freezing, stopping rigor.
questions.explain: A complete absence of rigor implies that either it hasn't started yet (less than 2 hours dead) or the muscle fibers have begun to autolyze and the rigor has fully faded away (greater than 36-48 hours dead).
questions.exam: HOSA Forensic Science: Crime Scene & Death Investigation
questions.subject: Forensic Science

questions.q: According to general postmortem guidelines for algor mortis, approximately what is the standard rate of temperature loss per hour for the first 12 hours after death?
questions.explain: In Fahrenheit, a typical human body cools at an average rate of $1.4^{\circ}F$ ($0.78^{\circ}C$) per hour for the first 12 hours.
questions.exam: HOSA Forensic Science: Crime Scene & Death Investigation
questions.subject: Forensic Science

questions.q: Calculate the estimated time of death using algor mortis: A victim is found with a core body temperature of $84.6^{\circ}F$. Assuming normal body temperature is $98.6^{\circ}F$ and the body has cooled at standard rates, how long has the person been dead?
questions.explain: Total temperature loss = $98.6 - 84.6 = 14.0^{\circ}F$. Since the loss is under the first 12-hour maximum ($12 \times 1.4 = 16.8^{\circ}F$), we divide $14.0 / 1.4 = 10$ hours.
questions.exam: HOSA Forensic Science: Crime Scene & Death Investigation
questions.subject: Forensic Science

questions.q: Calculate the estimated time of death using algor mortis: A body's internal temperature is $78.0^{\circ}F$. Assuming normal body temperature is $98.6^{\circ}F$, standard cooling rates ($1.4^{\circ}F$/hr for first 12 hrs, $0.7^{\circ}F$/hr thereafter), how many hours ago did death occur? (Round to one decimal place).
questions.explain: Total loss = $98.6 - 78.0 = 20.6^{\circ}F$. Loss in first 12 hrs = $12 \times 1.4 = 16.8^{\circ}F$. Remaining loss = $20.6 - 16.8 = 3.8^{\circ}F$. Time for remaining loss at $0.7^{\circ}F$/hr = $3.8 / 0.7 \approx 5.4$ hours. Total PMI = $12 + 5.4 = 17.4$ hours.
questions.exam: HOSA Forensic Science: Crime Scene & Death Investigation

questions.q: How is a deceased victim's core body temperature most accurately measured by an investigator at a crime scene?
options: Using a laser surface thermometer on the forehead.
Taking the temperature via the rectum or liver.
Placing a thermometer in the armpit.
questions.explain: To obtain an accurate internal (core) body temperature for calculating algor mortis, investigators must insert a thermometer directly into the liver or rectum.
questions.exam: HOSA Forensic Science: Crime Scene & Death Investigation
questions.subject: Forensic Science

questions.q: Which combination of environmental and physiological factors would accelerate the onset and rate of rigor mortis?
options: A naked body found in an extremely cold snowbank.
A heavy individual who died peacefully in their sleep.
A victim who engaged in severe physical struggle in a hot environment prior to death.
A person submerged in an icy river.
questions.explain: High ambient temperatures and heavy exercise prior to death deplete ATP rapidly and increase body temperature, significantly accelerating the onset and completion of rigor mortis.
questions.exam: HOSA Forensic Science: Crime Scene & Death Investigation
questions.subject: Forensic Science

questions.q: In forensic entomology, which group of insects is typically the first to arrive and lay eggs on a deceased human body?
questions.explain: Blowflies have an exceptionally keen sense of smell for putrescine and cadaverine and are often the first insects to arrive at a corpse, sometimes within minutes of death.
questions.exam: HOSA Forensic Science: Crime Scene & Death Investigation
questions.subject: Forensic Science

questions.q: If investigators observe 'dual lividity' on a body, what does this indicate?
options: The victim had two entirely separate causes of death.
The victim was kept in one position for roughly 2-8 hours, then shifted to another position before lividity became fully permanent.
The victim bled out internally and externally.
The victim was frozen shortly after death.
questions.explain: Dual lividity (two separate patterns of pooling) occurs if a body is moved after lividity has begun to form but before it is completely fixed (i.e., between 2 and 8 hours postmortem).
questions.exam: HOSA Forensic Science: Crime Scene & Death Investigation
questions.subject: Forensic Science

questions.q: What does the acronym PMI stand for in the context of forensic death investigation?
questions.explain: PMI stands for Post-Mortem Interval, which is the estimated time that has elapsed since the person died.
